Pethor
PEE-thor
proper noun
A city of Mesopotamia, by the river Euphrates, the home of Balaam the son of Beor, the hireling prophet whom Balak sent for to curse Israel; the name is taken to mean “interpreter of dreams” or “soothsaying.”

📖 Biblical Definition

Pethor was a city of Mesopotamia, by the river Euphrates, the home of Balaam the son of Beor. When Balak king of Moab feared the advancing hosts of Israel, “he sent messengers therefore unto Balaam the son of Beor to Pethor, which is by the river of the land of the children of his people, to call him” (Num 22:5), to come and curse Israel for reward. Balaam was a soothsayer who knew something of the true God, yet loved the wages of unrighteousness; and the whole account is a monument to the sovereignty of God over the tongues and schemes of men. Though Balaam came coveting the curse-money, God would not suffer him to curse: “the LORD thy God would not hearken unto Balaam; but the LORD thy God turned the curse into a blessing unto thee, because the LORD thy God loved thee” (Deu 23:5). Four times Balaam opened his mouth to curse, and four times God turned it to blessing. Yet Balaam, unable to curse, taught Balak the darker counsel of seducing Israel to sin at Baal-peor, and so is forever branded for “the way of Balaam…who loved the wages of unrighteousness” and for the doctrine that casts a stumblingblock before God’s people. Pethor thus stands for the covetous hireling in religion, whom God overrules for His people’s good even while judging his greed; no curse can light on those whom God has blessed.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A city of Mesopotamia, home of Balaam the hireling prophet; a monument that God turns the curse into blessing and overrules covetous schemes for His people’s good.

PETHOR, a city of Mesopotamia, by the river Euphrates.

It was the home of Balaam the son of Beor, the hireling prophet.

Balak sent there to fetch Balaam to curse Israel (Num 22:5).

God turned the intended curse into a blessing (Deu 23:5).

Balaam is branded for loving the wages of unrighteousness.

📖 Key Scripture

Num 22:5 — "He sent messengers therefore unto Balaam the son of Beor to Pethor, which is by the river of the land of the children of his people, to call him, saying, Behold, there is a people come out from Egypt: behold, they cover the face of the earth, and they abide over against me:"

Deu 23:5 — "Nevertheless the LORD thy God would not hearken unto Balaam; but the LORD thy God turned the curse into a blessing unto thee, because the LORD thy God loved thee."

Jud 1:11 — "Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core."

Rev 2:14 — "But I have a few things against thee, because thou hast there them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel, to eat things sacrificed unto idols, and to commit fornication."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A city of Scripture whose prophet embodies covetous, hireling religion; it recovers the truth that God turns the curse into blessing and no curse can light on His people.

expand to see more

Pethor and its prophet name a live and abiding corruption: the way of Balaam, the covetous hireling in religion who loves the wages of unrighteousness, and who, unable to curse God’s people outright, seeks to seduce them into sin. His doctrine, casting a stumblingblock before the saints, is warned against to the very churches of Revelation.

Yet the deeper truth of Pethor is the sovereignty of God over every curse and scheme. He would not suffer Balaam to curse, but turned the curse into a blessing, because He loved His people. No enchantment prospers against Jacob, no divination against Israel; and the believer rests in a God who overrules the greed and malice of men, so that no curse can finally light upon those whom He has blessed in Christ.
